questions.question: What is debenture in capital market? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is debenture in capital market? [U] / [CO1]
  • A debenture is a long-term debt instrument issued by companies to raise capital from the public.
  • It carries a fixed rate of interest and is repayable after a specified period. Debenture holders are
  • creditors of the company and do not have ownership rights.

questions.question: Name two types of general insurance policies. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Name two types of general insurance policies. [K] / [CO2]
  • Fire insurance and marine insurance are two common types of general insurance policies. Fire
  • insurance covers losses due to fire accidents, while marine insurance covers risks related to sea
  • transport and cargo.

questions.question: What is the role of the National Stock Exchange of India in the Indian stock market? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the role of the National Stock Exchange of India in the Indian stock market?
  • [K] / [CO3]
  • National Stock Exchange of India provides a transparent and efficient platform for trading
  • securities in India. It facilitates buying and selling of shares through electronic trading systems.
  • The exchange also helps in price discovery and investor protection.

questions.question: In which year was LIC established? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• In which year was LIC established? [K] / [CO2]
  • Life Insurance Corporation of India was established in the year 1956. It was formed after the
  • nationalization of the life insurance business in India.

questions.question: How does ICICI help small and medium enterprises through its investment pattern? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• How does ICICI help small and medium enterprises through its investment pattern?
  • [U] / [CO2]
  • ICICI Bank supports small and medium enterprises by providing loans, working capital
  • finance, and investment assistance. It also offers advisory and digital banking services to
  • improve business growth. These financial services help SMEs expand operations and improve
  • productivity.

questions.question: Why do companies pay dividends to shareholders? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why do companies pay dividends to shareholders? [U] / [CO3]
  • Companies pay dividends to distribute a portion of profits to shareholders as a return on their
  • investment. Dividends increase investor confidence and attract more investments. They also
  • reflect the financial strength and profitability of the company.

questions.question: How does IFCI support industrial development? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• How does IFCI support industrial development? [U] / [CO2]
  • Industrial Finance Corporation of India supports industrial development by providing long -
  • term financial assistance to industries and infrastructure projects. It offers loans, underwriting,
  • and project financing services. IFCI also promo tes entrepreneurship and industrial growth in
  • India.

questions.question: Who regulates credit rating agencies in India? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Who regulates credit rating agencies in India? [U] / [CO2]
  • Securities and Exchange Board of India regulates credit rating agencies in India. SEBI ensures
  • that rating agencies operate transparently and follow proper guidelines and standards.

questions.question: Why must investors register before filing a complaint on SCORES? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Why must investors register before filing a complaint on SCORES? [K] / [CO4]
  • Investors must register on SCORES to authenticate their identity and track complaints
  • effectively. Registration helps SEBI maintain proper re cords and communication with
  • investors. It also ensures transparency and efficient grievance redressal.

questions.question: Why do investors study a company’s financial statements? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why do investors study a company’s financial statements? [K] / [CO3]
  • Investors study financial statements to evaluate the profitability, liquidity, and financial
  • stability of a company. These statements help them make informed investment decisions.
  • Financial analysis also assists in assessing the future growth potential of the company.

questions.question: Explain the main objectives of SEBI in regulating the capital market. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the main objectives of SEBI in regulating the capital market. [U] / [CO1]
  • The main objective of Securities and Exchange Board of India is to protect the interests of
  • investors in the capital market. SEBI regulates stock exchanges and market intermediaries to
  • ensure fair and transparent trading practices. It also prom otes the orderly development of the
  • securities market.

questions.question: What is credit rating in finance? / [CO2] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• What is credit rating in finance? [U] / [CO2]
  • Credit rating is the assessment of the creditworthiness and repayment capacity of a borrower
  • or financial instrument. It indicates the level of risk associated with lending or investing. Higher
  • credit ratings reflect lower default risk and greater financial stability.

questions.question: What is the risk level in intraday trading compared to swing trading? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the risk level in intraday trading compared to swing trading? [U] / [CO3]
  • Intraday trading involves buying and selling securities within the same trading day and carries
  • a high level of risk. Price fluctuations in a short period can lead to quick gains or heavy losses.
  • Swing trading involves holding securities for several days or weeks to benefit from medium -
  • term price movements. Compared to swing trading, intraday trading is more risky due to market
  • volatility and rapid decision -making. Therefore, intraday traders require greater market
  • knowledge and risk management skills.

questions.question: How does a Ponzi scheme use money from new investors to pay old investors? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• How does a Ponzi scheme use money from new investors to pay old investors? [U] /
  • [CO4]
  • A Ponzi scheme is a fraudulent investment scheme wh ere returns to earlier investors are paid
  • using funds collected from new investors. The scheme does not generate genuine profits
  • through business or investment activities. It creates a false impression of high returns to attract
  • more participants. As long as new investors continue to join, payments can be maintained
  • temporarily. However, the scheme eventually collapses when new investments decline.

questions.question: What does a fall in the Sensex indicate? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What does a fall in the Sensex indicate? [U] / [CO3]
  • A fall in the BSE Sensex indicates a decline in the pri ces of major listed companies on the
  • stock market. It reflects negative investor sentiment and reduced market confidence. A
  • declining Sensex may result from economic uncertainty, poor corporate performance, or global
  • financial issues. It can also indicate lower demand for shares in the market. Thus, the fall of
  • the Sensex generally signals weakness in the stock market.

questions.question: What is the difference between Open-ended and Closed-ended Mutual Funds? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the difference between Open-ended and Closed-ended Mutual Funds? [K] /
  • [CO1]
  • Open-ended mutual funds allow investors to buy and sell units at any time from the fund itself.
  • These funds do not have a fixed maturity period and provide high liquidity. Closed -ended
  • mutual funds have a fixed maturity period and a limited number of units issued at the time of
  • launch. Investors generally bu y or sell units of closed -ended funds through stock exchanges.
  • Therefore, open-ended funds are more flexible compared to closed-ended funds.

questions.question: What types of financial instruments does Unit Trust of India invest in? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What types of financial instruments does Unit Trust of India invest in? [K] / [CO2]
  • Unit Trust of India invests i n various financial instruments such as equity shares, debentures,
  • bonds, and money market instruments. It also invests in government securities and corporate
  • debt instruments. These investments help generate returns for unit holders while maintaining
  • portfolio diversification. UTI selects instruments based on risk and return considerations. Its
  • investments contribute to capital market development and investor wealth creation.

questions.question: What types of financial assistance does IDBI provide? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What types of financial assistance does IDBI provide? [U] / [CO2]
  • Industrial Development Bank of India provides long -term and short-term financial assistance
  • to industries and businesses. It offers project finance, working capital assistance, underwriting,
  • and refinancing services. IDBI also supports infrastructure development and in dustrial
  • modernization projects. The institution provides technical and advisory support to
  • entrepreneurs and industries. These services help promote industrial growth and economic
  • development.

questions.question: How can grievance redressal systems increase confidence in the market? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• How can grievance redressal systems increase confidence in the market? [K] / [CO4]
  • Grievance redressal systems help investors resolve complaints related to fraud, unfair practices,
  • or service deficiencies. Effective complaint handling increases transparency and accountability
  • in financial markets. Investors feel more secure when they know their concerns will be
  • addressed properly. Such systems also improve the reputation and credibility of market
  • institutions. Therefore, grievance redressal mechanisms stren gthen investor confidence and
  • market stability.

questions.question: How can responsible investing reduce financial risks? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• How can responsible investing reduce financial risks? [K] / [CO4]
  • Responsible investing considers environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors along
  • with financial performance. Companies following su stainable and ethical practices are
  • generally exposed to lower legal, reputational, and operational risks. ESG -based investments
  • help investors avoid businesses involved in environmental damage or governance failures.
  • Responsible investing also supports long-term financial stability and sustainable growth. Thus,
  • it reduces potential financial losses and investment risks.

questions.question: How do RBI, NSE, and BSE together support the Indian economy? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• How do RBI, NSE, and BSE together support the Indian economy? [U] / [CO1]
  • Reserve Bank of India regulates the monetary and banking syste m to maintain economic
  • stability. National Stock Exchange of India and Bombay Stock Exchange provide organized
  • platforms for trading securities and mobilizing capital. Together, these institutions promote
  • investment, liquidity, and efficient allocation of financial resources. They ensure transparency,
  • investor protection, and smooth functioning of financial markets. Their combined role
  • contributes significantly to economic growth and financial development in India.

questions.question: How does CARE contribute to transparency in financial markets? / [CO2] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• How does CARE contribute to transparency in financial markets? [K] / [CO2]
  • CARE Ratings contributes to transparency by providing independent credit ratings for
  • companies and financial instruments. These ratings help investors assess the creditworthiness
  • and risk level of investments. CARE improves the availability of reliable financial information
  • in the market. Its ratings assist lenders, investors, and regulators in making informed decisions.
  • Thus, CARE enhances trust, transparency, and efficiency in financial markets.
